situation: early: out of stealth Jul 22, 2026 with $180M at a $1.2B valuation; founded 2025; ~100 employees; a handful of named customers; category name not settled (company_profile.json)
finding_pattern: absent (secondary: misrepresented on Gemini via look-alike 'Glow' companies)
angle: When a buyer describes the problem Glow solves without naming Glow, AI answers with someone else every time; and when they do name Glow, Gemini often describes a different company called Glow.

lead_claims.figure: Gemini says Glow does not claim ISO 27001 in 2 answers (main and follow-up, prompt #9), quoting getglow.ai; trust.glow.io lists ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2
33 of 34 blind conversations name another vendor; 10 name only tools the buyer already owns
Glow recommended outright in 2 of 12 head-to-head answers (16.7%)

opener.text: Congrats on the AWS Security Agent finding. Two CVEs for tools that could hand a scanned codebase, credentials included, to an attacker's bucket is a sharp catch.
opener.source_facts: Glow Labs post, Nov 17, 2026: AWS Security Agent plugin and MCP server could upload a workspace's source archive, which can include credentials, to a pre-created S3 bucket owned by a third party; CVE-2026-87912 and CVE-2026-87913; AWS published fixes. Read live 2026-11-20 (WebFetch).
opener.why_this_opener: Most recent dated Glow milestone (3 days old), specific to Glow, and it bridges naturally: research is how buyers first hear a new security name, which is the question the audit answers. Considered and rejected: the Aug 31 CISO appointment (nearly three months old) and the 7AI partnership (Nov 10, shared announcement).

run_size.note: Google AI Mode didn't return answers this cycle.

contacts.name: Roi Tiger
sources: research.json dossier 'Founders and leadership' (glow.io launch release, TechCrunch, Globes, Redpoint)

email.note: No real @glow.io address found in public sources (the launch release, the CISO announcement and search results show none; Prospeo's 'Glow Security' email-format page is a different, 1-10 person company in Ohio). Candidates are common startup patterns, not observed; the sponsor verifies with Hunter before sending.

rationale: Glow is four months out of stealth and its story is still being written, so the audit leads with being understood at all. AI never brings Glow up when a buyer describes the problem (0 of 68 blind answers), and in the vendor-risk check that runs alongside the technical evaluation Gemini answers with a different company called Glow and says it lacks ISO 27001. Glow's leadership comes from security and trust (a CISO-led trust function, a COO who was a CISO), so that finding should land. The opener uses this week's Glow Labs AWS disclosure because research is exactly how Glow is earning attention, and the email's question is whether that attention reaches AI answers. The email asks for nothing beyond whether the full report is useful. Email address is unverified; check with Hunter before sending.
